clue.text: University leader's bad luck when revolution returns

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: vice is wickedness, something bad
chance means luck or fortune

indicators.note: returns signals that the word for a turn is read back to front

parts.note: a roll is one turn over, a revolution

explanation.surface: A university head suffers misfortune when an uprising comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns ROLL into LLOR at the end. In British universities the vice-chancellor is the working head, the chancellor being largely ceremonial.
explanation.definitionFit: In British universities the chief executive officer holds this title.

clue.text: Composition of Queen Elizabeth suite (1558) shows plausibility

indicators.note: composition is putting together, so the letters are assembled afresh

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the royal cipher
1558 in Roman numerals is MDLVIII

explanation.surface: A piece of music for Elizabeth I, dated to her accession year, sounds convincing.
explanation.walkthrough: 1558 is the year Elizabeth I came to the throne, which makes the surface feel historical; the number is just Roman numerals MDLVIII to be mixed with ER and SUITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Verisimilitude is the appearance of being true or real, i.e. believability.

clue.text: Food for the house

definitions.meaning: provisions or rations shared at a common table, as in college
the House of ..., the lower chamber of the UK Parliament

explanation.surface: Something to eat for the household.
explanation.definitionFit: Commons means shared rations, and is also the British lower parliamentary chamber.

clue.text: Plant smart sum of money on Guardianeditor

parts.note: chic means smart or stylish
K stands for a thousand, a sum of money
printed as one word: Guardian gives WE, how the paper refers to itself, and editor gives ED

explanation.surface: Bet a stylish amount of cash on the newspaper's editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb (to place a bet) but is the definition. The Guardian setter uses WE for the paper itself; 'on' means placed after, in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Chickweed is a common small white-flowered weed, a plant.

clue.text: Sex hormone replaced on gander

indicators.note: replaced means put in a different place, so the letters move around

explanation.surface: A male goose has been given a substitute sex hormone.
explanation.walkthrough: A gander is a male goose, which suits a male hormone.
explanation.definitionFit: Androgens such as testosterone are the male sex hormones.

clue.text: University house in South Island

definitions.meaning: the Oxford college known familiarly as the House
a city in the South Island of New Zealand

explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford college shares its name with the largest city on New Zealand's South Island.

clue.text: House of cricket

parts.note: both the upper chamber of Parliament and the London ground called the home of cricket

explanation.definitionFit: The House of Lords is a parliamentary chamber; Lord's is cricket's headquarters ground in London.

clue.text: First in musical house

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the musical's name

parts.note: Oliver! is the Lionel Bart stage musical
I is the Roman numeral one, first

explanation.surface: The leading role in a show staged at a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The Olivier is one of the theatres (houses) at the National Theatre in London, named after Laurence Olivier.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre is called a house, and the Olivier is a National Theatre auditorium.

clue.text: Any old chum I let off any old how

indicators.note: off means not right, so these letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Any old friend I let go, without care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Any old' appears in both fodder and definition, which hides where the split falls.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something any old how means doing it without system or method.

clue.text: Note without a rest

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the note goes around the letter

parts.note: a reminder is a note to jog the memory

explanation.surface: A musical note played without any pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' and 'rest' look like music, but a note is a memo and 'without' means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is what is left over, the rest.

clue.text: Start to light again as a rule

indicators.note: only the start of the word is taken, dropping its last three letters

parts.note: to reignite is to set alight once more

explanation.surface: Usually, one relights something.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the front part of REIGNITE is used, dropping ITE; 'as a' links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's reign is the period or fact of ruling.

clue.text: House and family with old coppers?

parts.note: stock is lineage or ancestry
ex means former
copper coins are small change

explanation.surface: A household with family and some old policemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police, but it is copper coins, i.e. change. The London Stock Exchange is traditionally called the House.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stock Exchange is traditionally nicknamed the House by those who work there.

clue.text: One of fixed ideas makes bosses' problem setter's

indicators.note: a problem is something tangled, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the possessive apostrophe adds no letter
the setter has: I've

explanation.surface: Managers' difficulties make the puzzle-setter fixated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' looks like a noun belonging to the bosses, but it signals the jumble; a setter refers to themself as 'I', so 'setter's' is 'I have' shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsessive person is someone dominated by fixed ideas.

clue.text: Collected and keen type, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: Keen's is a brand of mustard, and keen as mustard is an idiom

explanation.surface: Gathered together and an enthusiastic person, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops are mustered when they are assembled or gathered.

clue.text: See 5
Is pigeon talk interrupting aid from aerial rescuer?

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so these go inside the other word

parts.note: help means aid
coo is the sound pigeons make

explanation.surface: Is a pigeon's cooing disturbing help coming from a helicopter?
explanation.definitionFit: This is a rescue device lowered from a helicopter, so an aerial rescuer.

clue.text: See 11
Sex drive to order in cat with no tail?

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other
with no tail means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a lion is a big cat
to bid is to order or command

explanation.surface: Is a cat lacking a tail driven to mate on command?
explanation.walkthrough: The cat loses its last letter to give LIO, which holds BID.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is sexual desire or drive.

clue.text: Spooner's received disapproval of further writing

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of the two words

parts.note: took means received
boo is a noise of disapproval

explanation.surface: Spooner got jeered for writing more.
explanation.walkthrough: TOOK BOO swaps to BOOK TOO, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A second volume is further writing following the first.

clue.text: Went to discover what could be 10 or 50 deep

indicators.note: what could be signals that the letters could be rearranged into something else

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten
L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: Investigated whether something was ten or fifty deep.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference to the clue at 10 across, but it is just X.
explanation.definitionFit: To explore is to travel somewhere to find out about it.

clue.text: Carroty stuff may get one harried

indicators.note: may get suggests one set of letters can be turned into another

explanation.surface: Ginger hair can get a person harassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is a link; the anagram indicator 'may get' sits between definition and fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroty describes orange-red hair, so carroty stuff is ginger hair.

clue.text: Doll having meal outside — that's after hurtful remark

indicators.note: after means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: a barb is a cutting remark
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A doll eating out after someone made a cutting comment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having meal outside' is an extra hint: barbie is Australian slang for a barbecue.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbie is the famous fashion doll made by Mattel.

clue.text: Prime minister: "Good conduct is for everyone"

parts.note: Tao, the way in Chinese philosophy, means right conduct
taken as written
each means for every one

explanation.surface: A prime minister's slogan says good behaviour applies to all.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taoiseach is the prime minister of Ireland.

clue.text: Relative conceals expression of satisfaction, being a gentleman

indicators.note: conceals means holds inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a sib is a sibling, a relative
ah is a sigh of contentment

explanation.surface: A relative hides contentment at being a gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Sahib was a respectful Indian title for a gentleman or master.

clue.text: Containing Na, thus upsetting police

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: upsetting means turning over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Thus overturning the police.
explanation.walkthrough: Na is the chemical symbol for sodium.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodic means containing sodium, whose chemical symbol is Na.

clue.text: Wife sharing cost of meal?

definitions.meaning: in Cockney slang my old ... is one's wife
going ... means each person paying their own share

explanation.definitionFit: Cockney slang calls a wife one's old Dutch; going Dutch means splitting a bill.

clue.text: House to house collector of rubbish: objective, keeping hospital student

parts.note: a bin collects rubbish

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside

parts.note: a goal is an objective
L for learner, a student driver's plate

explanation.surface: Each house a dustman visits is his aim, including the hospital and a student.
explanation.walkthrough: In bingo the winner shouts 'House!', so a bingo hall is a place to house House.
explanation.definitionFit: A bingo hall is a building where the game nicknamed House is played.

clue.text: Feature of the hajj: pray Deo — badly? Try again in that case

parts.note: the word hajj contains two J's together

indicators.note: badly means poorly arranged, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A pilgrim prays to God poorly, so may have to repeat it.
explanation.walkthrough: Double jeopardy is the legal bar on being tried twice for the same offence; the definition describes what it forbids.
explanation.definitionFit: Double jeopardy is the legal situation of being tried a second time for the same crime.
